A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cooperative stochastic bandit research, with shared authors, model, algorithms, and regret analysis. The main text, mathematical material, displays, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization and extensions.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, theoretical regret bounds, and proofs. Neither the main text nor appendices contain original experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Table 1 compares analytical guarantees, and the NeurIPS checklist explicitly confirms that the paper contains no experiments.

M1.justification: V2 introduces Coop-SE-Comm-Cost, using growing tree clusters and phased information gathering, synchronization, and sampling (Algorithms 4 and 13). Main Coop-SE and the CONGEST variant now select actions round-robin rather than uniformly. Round-robin was already mentioned in v1 Remark 1, and the randomized variant remains in v2 Appendix F. Coop-SE-CONGEST develops the existing Coop-SE-Low-Comm rather than being entirely new.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or executes training or evaluation scenarios. V2's additional communication constraints and graph examples are theoretical settings, not empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. V2 Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees for Coop-UCB2, DDUCB, UCB-TCOM, and the proposed variants; this changes research positioning rather than evaluated baseline membership.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures. Changes to mathematical communication models and assumptions are covered under M1 and T1.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses. The additional graph arguments and algorithm analyses in v2 are formal theoretical developments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. Algorithmic confidence bounds and probabilistic proof events do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores, rankings, or qualitative experimental outcomes. Added and revised analytical regret and communication bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix E supplies the round-robin analysis omitted in v1 Remark 1 and adds a diameter-sensitive refinement in Theorem 7. Appendix H.2 introduces clustering lemmas and amortized regret and communication-count proofs for the new phased algorithm. The CONGEST guarantees are revised, including the claimed message bound from O(log(mTA)) to O(log(mA)). Section 2 adds the assumption m, A <= poly(T). V1's randomized analysis is retained in Appendix F.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds the randomized minimax guarantee; v2 foregrounds the round-robin, instance-dependent guarantee while retaining the randomized result. V2 adds a principal claim of O(log(T)) communication rounds with regret O(R log(A)/m + A log(A) log(T)), where R is the single-agent gap-dependent bound. It also explicitly reframes the core contribution as a new analysis of an existing cooperative SE variant.

C2.justification: V2 adds qualifications about when randomized selection improves the bound, why the main lower bound concerns the existence of a hard agent, and how diameter terms behave on grids and cycles. Section 8 identifies simultaneously achieving small messages and few communication rounds as unresolved. The central interpretation of diameter independence and the open additive dependence on A remain.

D1.justification: V2 makes the empirical-mean input explicit in detailed Coop-SE pseudocode, revises message fields to omit certain timestamps, and adds field-by-field message-size accounting in Lemma 25. Algorithms 4 and 12–13 document clustering, counters, and forwarding for the new protocol. Neither version supplies executable code, hardware details, or runtime measurements.

R1.justification: New Section 1.3 explicitly connects Coop-SE to prior cooperative SE algorithms by Yang and Zhang and limits the novelty claim to its analysis. The earlier claim of resolving Kolla's question becomes a complementary contribution. Section 1.4 and Table 1 substantially expand comparisons of graph dependence, communication, and required graph knowledge, with added references including Zhang et al. and distributed averaging work.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution narrative, proof sketch, communication discussion, and concluding section are extensively rewritten. The warm-up proof moves to Appendix D, additional related work to Appendix A, and the retained randomized analysis to Appendix F. Appendices are reorganized around separate algorithm variants, and a NeurIPS checklist is added.

P2.justification: V2 adds the multi-column theoretical comparison Table 1 and removes v1 Figure 1 illustrating implicit synchronization. Main-text algorithm displays are substantially simplified, detailed algorithms are regrouped in Appendix J, and new algorithm boxes are added. NeurIPS typesetting changes typography, title treatment, spacing, and display placement throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves theoretical completeness by developing the round-robin result that v1 left without proof and providing a constructive protocol and detailed analysis for limited communication rounds. Its explicit acknowledgment of prior cooperative SE algorithms also makes the contribution more precise. A drawback is the new abstract's omission of the log(A) factor present in Theorem 5 and the contribution list. This reporting inconsistency does not outweigh the substantial gains in analytical support and research positioning.
